title: 25-Minute Lock In
short: Phone in another room. 25 minutes on your most important task.
why: One protected block is how the important thing actually moves.
how: Pick the one task that matters most today.
Put your phone in another room.
Start the 25:00 timer and stay on that one task.
proof: Your workspace or notes after the timer.

title: Get One Win Before Noon
short: Finish one thing you've been putting off before 12.
why: A win early sets the pace for the rest of the day.
how: Pick something small you keep pushing back.

title: Plan Tomorrow Tonight
short: Write your three most important tasks for tomorrow.
why: You start faster when the first decision is already made.
how: Before bed, write tomorrow's top three on paper.

title: Finish Something
short: Pick one unfinished task, assignment or project and finish it.
why: Half-done things cost you every time you think about them.
how: Pick the one that's closest to done.
Work until it's finished, not until you're tired.

title: Study Sprint
short: One subject, 25 focused minutes.
why: Short, focused sessions beat long, distracted ones.

title: 10 Pages
short: Read at least 10 pages of a book.
why: Ten pages a day is about a book a month.

title: Start Before It's Urgent
short: Work 40 minutes on something that isn't due today.
why: Starting early is the difference between a draft and a panic.
how: Pick the next big thing due.
Get a rough first part done.
proof: The draft or work you got done.

title: Teach It Back
short: Write a short explanation of something you learned today.
why: If you can explain it simply, you actually know it.
how: Pick one thing from class or a video.
Explain it in 5 sentences on paper, notes closed.

title: Move for 20
short: Walk, run or work out for at least 20 minutes.
why: Twenty minutes of moving does more for your energy than another coffee.
how: Pick walk, run or a workout.
proof: Where you moved, after the timer.

title: Get Outside
short: Spend 10 minutes outside.
why: Daylight and air reset your head faster than a scroll.

title: Mobility Reset
short: Stretch or do mobility work for 10 minutes.
why: Tight hips and back come from sitting. Ten minutes undoes a lot of it.
proof: Your stretch spot after the timer.

title: Train Today
short: Do a full 40-minute workout.
why: Strength comes from showing up and doing the work, not the perfect plan.
how: Pick your workout: gym or bodyweight.
proof: Your workout spot or equipment after.

title: Know Where Your Money Went
short: Write down everything you spent today.
why: Money disappears in small amounts you don't remember.
how: Write each purchase and add it up.
proof: Your handwritten list. No bank info.

title: Career Skill: 20 Minutes
short: Spend 20 minutes learning a skill people pay for.
why: Skills compound. Twenty minutes a day adds up fast.
how: Pick one skill: spreadsheets, design, writing, code.
Start the 20:00 timer and follow one lesson.
proof: Your workspace or course after the timer.

title: Apply
short: Apply for one job, internship or scholarship.
why: Every yes started as an application someone almost didn't send.
how: Fill it out and send it.

title: Money Plan
short: Write what you'll save and spend this week.
why: A plan on paper beats a guess every time.
how: Write what's coming in this week.
Write what you'll save first, then what you'll spend.
proof: Your plan on paper. No account numbers.

title: Build for 30
short: 30 minutes on your project: art, music, code, a brand, anything.
why: Projects get built in small sessions, not in your head.
how: Work on it and nothing else.

title: Ship Something
short: Finish one small part of your project instead of planning it.
why: Finished beats perfect. You can't improve what doesn't exist.
how: Pick one piece you can finish today.

title: Create 1 Thing
short: Make one small thing: a sketch, a beat, a paragraph, a design.
why: Making something small every day is how you get good.

title: Improve Yesterday's Work
short: Take something you made and make it better.
why: The second pass is where it gets good.

title: Make the Bed
short: Make your bed before you leave the room.
why: The first thing you finish today. Takes two minutes.
how: Feet on the floor, then the bed.

title: Reset Your Desk
short: Clear trash, dishes and clutter off your desk.
why: Clean the desk. Clear your head.
how: Trash out, dishes back, stuff away.
proof: Before and after of the desk.

title: 10-Minute Room Reset
short: Clean one part of your room for 10 minutes.
why: Ten minutes a day stops it turning into a whole-weekend job.
how: Ten minutes, then the after photo.
proof: Before and after of that area.

title: Tomorrow Is Ready
short: Pack your bag and set out what you need for tomorrow.
why: Mornings go wrong the night before.
how: Set out clothes and anything you need.

title: Write the Move
short: Write one thing you're avoiding and the first action to start it.
why: Avoiding is usually not knowing the first step.
how: Write the first action, small enough to do today.

title: Make the Decision
short: Pick something you've been overthinking and write your decision.
why: Not deciding is a decision too, just a worse one.
how: Write what you're picking and why, in two lines.

title: Do the Small Version
short: Take the first real step on something you've delayed.
why: The small version is how big things actually start.
how: Pick the thing you keep delaying.
Do the smallest real version of it today.
proof: The result of the first step.

title: Ask for Help
short: Ask someone who knows for help with something you're stuck on.
why: Asking takes thirty seconds. Being stuck takes weeks.
how: Pick the person: teacher, coach, manager, older friend.
Ask in person or by message.
proof: Your note of what they said.
